bucket: circle entries document more administrative and governance dysfunction in concrete policies and procedures (unresponsive offices, punitive/inconsistent discipline policies, nepotism/favoritism, grade manipulation or exam/tuition enforcement, residency/credit transfer problems, and record-keeping errors) than square entries
definition: This bucket groups operational governance failures called out in circle reviews — e.g., exams withheld for late tuition, 'lost credits' on transfer, residency enforcement and cross-border enrollment disputes, accusations of grade‑alteration pressure, named rude front‑office staff, and calls for district/board accountability — distinguishing procedural and policy breakdowns from classroom- or program-level issues.

bucket: circle entries report more pervasive student-safety and disciplinary breakdowns (bullying, fights, gangs, sexual harassment, substance use) and more frequent failure to remediate them than square entries
definition: This bucket captures reports that the school climate itself is unsafe or violent and that adults do not fix it — e.g., Circle reviewers describe 'bullying almost every day,' 'fights every week,' 'gang activity,' sexual harassment, rampant drugs/alcohol and accounts that 'teachers/administration brush it under the rug' or 'encouraged' bullying; Square reviews lack or downplay these recurring safety incidents and often describe better administrative handling of specific bullying cases.

bucket: circle entries report stronger and more extensive advanced academic programs, college‑preparation pathways, CTE/dual‑enrollment and measurable student outcomes than square entries
definition: This groups concrete programmatic strengths attributed to circle schools: broad AP/honors offerings, high AP pass rates, sustained honors pathways, dual‑enrollment/High‑Tech/CTE academies, documented college credits and scholarships, organized senior supports (monthly scholarship updates, exit interviews) and third‑party rankings. These are program‑level, measurable offerings/outcomes (courses, credits, awards, counseling) rather than general feelings about staff, and appear far more often in circle reviews than in square.

bucket: circle entries report more concrete operational, facility, and day‑to‑day student support failures and inconsistencies (food safety, transportation, pest/mold, lost records, IEP/counseling problems, aftercare costs) than square entries
definition: Circle reviews provide many specific operational complaints and service breakdowns — cafeteria hazards and food poisoning, wasp infestations and mold, bus safety and busing not set up, lost medical/registration records, IEP non‑compliance and poor counseling, and punitive materials/transfer policies (e.g., 'found styrofoam in my burrito,' 'infested with wasps,' 'my son's medical documents were lost three times,' 'If you have a child with an IEP you will have a difficult time'). Square entries do not exhibit this concentration of concrete facilities/operational failures, so this bucket groups those tangible day‑to‑day service issues where circle > square.

bucket: circle entries report stronger community/parental/alumni engagement and richer localized extracurricular identity (small-town family continuity, active parent/alumni mobilization, celebrated band/arts/FFA/vocational programs and student-driven clubs) than square entries
definition: This covers social/co‑curricular strengths and community continuity — e.g., Circle reviewers repeatedly describe multi‑generational attendance, parents/alumni organizing against district actions, award‑winning band/FFA, many student‑initiated clubs and strong arts/athletics traditions and leadership opportunities; Square reviews emphasize mixed experiences, transfers, or do not portray the same level of entrenched local community investment.
